AInfCohomology:AI.0.title: Fontaine’s integral period rings
AInfCohomology:AI.0.summary: Construct A_inf from Witt vectors of a tilted valuation ring, together with Frobenius, the map to the original valuation ring and its kernel. Compare its crystalline and de Rham period-ring maps with their filtrations and twists.

AInfCohomology:AI.0:integral.title: A_inf, Frobenius and the Fontaine kernel
AInfCohomology:AI.0:integral.summary: Construct the integral period ring A_inf, its Frobenius and Fontaine map, and the distinguished kernel generators arising from compatible p-power roots of unity. Prove the required completeness, torsion and nonzerodivisor properties.

AInfCohomology:AI.0:period-comparison.title: Crystalline and de Rham period-ring maps
AInfCohomology:AI.0:period-comparison.summary: Compare the maps from A_inf to crystalline and de Rham period rings, including their Frobenius twists and defining ideals. Keep the divided-power and adic completion constructions distinct.

AInfCohomology:AI.7.title: Breuil–Kisin cohomology and descent
AInfCohomology:AI.7.summary: Construct Frobenius-equipped cohomology over W(k)[[u]] for smooth proper formal schemes over a complete discrete valuation ring. Compare its A_inf, de Rham and crystalline specializations, retaining the dependence on a uniformizer and possible cohomological torsion.

AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6.title: Homomorphisms, Rosati positivity and Weil restriction
AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6.summary: Study Hom and endomorphism groups of abelian varieties, Poincaré complete reducibility, Rosati positivity and polarized isogeny degrees. Construct Weil restriction and prove that finite étale restriction of an abelian scheme is again an abelian scheme.

AdelicAlgebraicGroups:AA.5.title: Ideles, modular quotients and quaternionic volumes
AdelicAlgebraicGroups:AA.5.summary: Identify adelic quotients for GL₁ with idele classes and the GL₂ rational case with upper-half-plane quotients. Compare compact definite quaternionic quotients and their volumes under changes of level.

AdicEtaleGeometry:A0.title: Completed tensor products and adic fibre products
AdicEtaleGeometry:A0.summary: Construct completed tensor products of compatible Huber pairs and their integral plus subrings. Prove the universal properties needed for adic fibre products, distinguishing separated completion from uniformization.

AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.title: Residual modularity and Serre weight and conductor
AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.summary: Define residual modularity through an eigenform and its residual Galois representation. Formulate Serre’s predicted weight and conductor, with determinant congruences and finite-flat weight-two consequences.

AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.title: Smooth compactification with normal-crossings boundary
AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.summary: For a smooth quasi-projective variety in characteristic zero, construct a smooth projective compactification preserving the original open variety and with strict normal-crossings complement. Over the complex numbers, describe the analytic polydisc charts used in extension theorems.

AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:N.title: Reconstruction of hyperbolic curves from fundamental groups
AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:N.summary: Reconstruct the specified smooth proper hyperbolic curves over number fields from outer Galois-equivariant fundamental-group data. Isomorphism and morphism versions retain their distinct hypotheses.

AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:N.title: Selmer varieties and Chabauty–Kim equations
AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:N.summary: Relate arithmetic fundamental-group reconstruction to Selmer varieties and iterated-integral equations for rational points. Describe finite Chabauty–Kim loci and the precision needed for their equations, retaining any motivic assumptions in conditional results.

AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4.title: Hecke and Artin L-functions and the class-number formula
AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4.summary: Relate ideal counting and Hecke characters to completed L-functions, the analytic class-number formula and Chebotarev estimates. Keep meromorphic continuation of Artin L-functions separate from the stronger holomorphy conjecture.

AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.6.title: Zero-free regions and conditional prime estimates
AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.6.summary: Apply zero-free regions, density estimates and explicit formulas to sieve and counting problems. Distinguish unconditional estimates from statements assuming the Riemann hypothesis, its generalizations or prime-pattern conjectures.

ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7.title: Tensor constructions and polarized Galois representations
ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:G7.summary: Construct exterior and symmetric powers, tensor induction and scalar restriction for continuous Galois representations. Develop polarizations, their signs and determinant constraints, together with the residual-image conditions used to choose auxiliary primes.

ArithmeticKTheory:N.8.title: Explicit K-groups of rational and quadratic fields
ArithmeticKTheory:N.8.summary: Compute low-degree K-groups for the integers, Gaussian integers and selected quadratic fields. Compare integral tame kernels with field K-groups and localization sequences for S-integers.

ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces:ALS.5.title: Finite-level Poincaré–Lefschetz duality
ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces:ALS.5.summary: Construct duality and compact-support pairings on arithmetic manifolds with corners, with orientation twists and perfect coefficient complexes. Prove compatibility with boundary triangles, level maps and Hecke adjoints, retaining the conditions needed when stabilizers occur.

ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces:ALS.6.title: Cohomology of arithmetic towers
ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces:ALS.6.summary: Assemble restriction, corestriction and Hecke actions across towers of arithmetic quotients. Compare finite-level descent with completed cohomology and boundary triangles, keeping derived inverse-limit terms.

ArithmeticQuantumTopology:QT.7.title: Quantum modularity and arithmetic asymptotic conjectures
ArithmeticQuantumTopology:QT.7.summary: Formulate quantum-modularity, refined-volume and arithmetic-resurgence statements with specified invariants and limiting regimes. Keep proved examples separate from conjectural families and numerical evidence.

ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5.title: Higher moments and local arithmetic distributions
ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5.summary: Study higher moments, local statistics, random-matrix models and function-field analogues of arithmetic distributions. Distinguish established asymptotic results from probabilistic models, with explicit convergence and uniformity conditions.

AutomorphicBundles:B1.general.title: Canonical principal bundles on general Shimura varieties
AutomorphicBundles:B1.general.summary: Construct the general canonical principal bundle and its compatibility with conjugation, extending beyond Hodge-type and abelian-type cases.

AutomorphicBundles:B2.general.title: Associated automorphic bundles and realizations
AutomorphicBundles:B2.general.summary: Form associated vector bundles from the general canonical principal bundle and the relevant algebraic representations. Compare their geometric realizations through the specified canonical maps.

AutomorphicBundles:B3.general.title: Canonical extensions over toroidal compactifications
AutomorphicBundles:B3.general.summary: Construct canonical and subcanonical extensions of general automorphic bundles over toroidal compactifications. Preserve logarithmic connections and the comparison maps between realizations.

AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.5.title: Hecke characters and classical modular forms
AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.5.summary: Identify GL₁ automorphic forms with Hecke characters and the GL₂ rational case with classical modular forms. Compare central characters, normalized Hecke operators and algebraic modular forms on groups compact at infinity.

AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:A.title: Invariant lattices and residual Galois representations
AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:A.summary: Choose invariant lattices after proving a coefficient field of realization, and compare their residual semisimplifications. Relate reductions of Frobenius polynomials to residual Hecke ideals, preserving the precise eigenvalue conditions at auxiliary primes.

AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL..title: Euler factors and critical-value normalization
AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL..summary: Compare primitive and imprimitive L-values, character twists and conductor exponents in the specified GL₂ and Rankin–Selberg families. Treat vanishing interpolation factors through explicit limiting or derivative formulas rather than cancellation.

AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L5.title: Periods, interpolation and p-adic L-function conjectures
AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L5.summary: Compare period choices, coefficient fields and Euler-factor conventions across the constructed p-adic L-functions. Formulate broader existence conjectures using explicit realizations, critical values and refinements without assuming their solutions.

BorelRegulators:R.1.title: Arithmetic groups and finite-type classifying spaces
BorelRegulators:R.1.summary: Study arithmetic groups arising from orders in division algebras through reduction theory and Borel–Serre compactification. Construct block inclusions and finite-type homotopy models needed for higher K-theory.

BorelRegulators:R.7.title: Borel–Beilinson regulator comparison
BorelRegulators:R.7.summary: Compare Borel and Beilinson–Deligne regulators with their exact normalization factors. Relate coordinate-free maps and regulator matrices, including low-rank examples over rational and imaginary quadratic fields.

ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:formal-a.title: Formal completion and étale specialization
ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:formal-a.summary: Construct specialization from an analytic generic fibre to the special fibre of a formal scheme and compute tube stalks. Compare cohomology near a closed subscheme with the cohomology of its formal completion under the stated finiteness hypotheses.

ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuatio.title: Valuation-base invariance and cohomology with supports
ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuatio.summary: Prove support comparisons and cohomological invariance for the specified surjective maps of valuation spectra. Establish constructibility and finiteness with the required presentation, dimension and boundary assumptions.

ClassicalArithmeticCompletion:CA.5.title: Integral bases, discriminants and ideal factorization
ClassicalArithmeticCompletion:CA.5.summary: Relate integral bases, units, class groups, relative discriminants and Frobenius to exact arithmetic computations. Compare matrix calculations with intrinsic number-field invariants in quadratic and cyclotomic examples.

ClassicalSerreModularity:R26.1.title: Serre modularity in level one
ClassicalSerreModularity:R26.1.summary: State the level-one residual modularity theorem with its classical Serre weight and all residual-characteristic cases. Identify the prescribed-lift and ramification-reduction statements needed for its proof and strengthened corollary.

ClassicalSerreModularity:R27.6.title: Serre’s weight-and-conductor modularity theorem
ClassicalSerreModularity:R27.6.summary: Produce a normalized newform of the predicted conductor and weight for each residual representation covered by classical Serre modularity. Prove determinant compatibility and coefficient-field invariance, including the finite-flat weight-two consequence.

ClassicalSerreModularity:R33.1.title: Weight reduction through compatible systems
ClassicalSerreModularity:R33.1.summary: Begin the qualitative Serre modularity argument by changing coefficient characteristic and obtaining a weight-two lift in a compatible system. Handle soluble and reducible branches with their separate local and residual-image hypotheses.

CohomologyComparisons:CP.0.title: Geometric fibres and period-ring comparison maps
CohomologyComparisons:CP.0.summary: Relate a formal scheme, its special fibre and its analytic generic fibre through their cohomological sites. Construct compatible crystalline, semistable and de Rham period-ring maps with Frobenius and Tate-twist conventions.

CohomologyComparisons:CP.6.title: Chern classes, products and p-adic comparison
CohomologyComparisons:CP.6.summary: Compare cup products, duals, traces and Chern classes across étale, de Rham, crystalline and prismatic cohomology. Derive the corresponding geometric Galois-representation statements with their integral, ramification and weight restrictions.

CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompati.title: Local–global compatibility and Fontaine–Mazur consequences
CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompati.summary: Formulate the local–global compatibility and support statements used in the specified modularity-lifting branches. Retain small-prime exceptions, local exclusions and the de Rham and oddness hypotheses needed for Fontaine–Mazur consequences.

CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.8.title: Galois and Hecke actions on completed cohomology
CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.8.summary: Compare completed cohomology with modular, Siegel, unitary and Hilbert tower models. Transport continuous Galois and Hecke actions through the level maps and localize at a residual Hecke ideal.

ComplexComparisonPartII:C6.title: GAGA and de Rham comparison in explicit geometries
ComplexComparisonPartII:C6.summary: Compute coherent and de Rham comparisons for projective space, infinitesimal thickenings, complex elliptic curves and the multiplicative group. Relate modular differentials, Hodge sections and isogeny graphs through their actual comparison maps.

ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciproc.title: Complex multiplication and reflex-norm reciprocity
ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciproc.summary: Compare complex-multiplication reciprocity with type and reflex norms. Identify ideal, idele and torsion actions while distinguishing the field of definition, endomorphism field and reflex field.

ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciproc.title: Class fields and torsion fields from complex multiplication
ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciproc.summary: Relate ring and ray class fields to torsion, Hecke characters and ideal actions in proved complex-multiplication cases. Describe the level functions that generate the asserted fields, with elliptic and higher-dimensional examples.

CrystallineCohomology:CR.3:duality.title: Crystalline trace and Poincaré duality
CrystallineCohomology:CR.3:duality.summary: Construct the trace and derived cup-product duality for proper smooth crystalline cohomology. Compare diagonal classes, Gysin maps and base change, retaining torsion through derived duals.

CrystallineCohomology:CR.7.title: Crystalline coefficients and Gauss–Manin connections
CrystallineCohomology:CR.7.summary: Relate crystals, connections, Frobenius and logarithmic monodromy to Dieudonné theory and deformation of p-divisible groups. Construct the finite-projective coefficient and relative Gauss–Manin comparisons needed for arithmetic families.

DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.10.title: Frobenius weights and arithmetic point-count bounds
DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.10.summary: Apply weights to Hecke-stable cohomological subquotients, duals and Tate twists, and derive point-count errors with the correct component contributions. Keep independence of the coefficient prime and broader weight–monodromy statements separate from basic purity.

DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.2.title: Purity for symplectic local systems
DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.2.summary: Prove the fundamental purity estimate for a local system on an open projective line with a nondegenerate alternating pairing, open geometric symplectic monodromy and rational local characteristic polynomials. Retain these hypotheses when extending coefficients.

DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.5.title: Local weights and monodromy on curves
DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.5.summary: Develop pure and mixed sheaves and their weight filtrations over finite fields. Prove the local weight theorem on curves, relating monodromy-graded pieces and boundary invariants to Frobenius weights.

DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5.title: Quasisyntomic descent and filtered cohomology
DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5.summary: Construct quasisyntomic sites and semiperfectoid covers, then prove descent for completed cotangent powers and derived de Rham cohomology. Establish the required filtered convergence, base-change and proper smooth perfectness results.

DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.6.title: Logarithmic cotangent and derived de Rham complexes
DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.6.summary: Construct logarithmic cotangent complexes and derived de Rham cohomology with their Hodge and conjugate filtrations. Compare logarithmic crystalline cohomology under the precise local-complete-intersection and Cartier-type hypotheses.

DiamondEtaleCohomology:C9.title: Compact objects in étale cohomology of diamonds
DiamondEtaleCohomology:C9.summary: Under uniform cohomological-dimension bounds, prove compact generation and identify compact objects in the derived étale category. Use bounded constructible complexes for finite-field coefficients and perfect-constructible complexes in the general coefficient setting.

DiamondSixOperations:S5.title: Cohomological smoothness of balls and quotients
DiamondSixOperations:S5.summary: Prove cohomological smoothness and normalized duality for the perfectoid ball, suitable profinite quotients and smooth analytic maps. Retain the prime-to-coefficient and quotient-representability hypotheses in each case.

DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence.title: Effective bounds for Thue and S-unit equations
DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence.summary: Apply lower bounds for linear forms in logarithms to Thue, Thue–Mahler, S-unit and exponential equations. Prove explicit height bounds that justify the remaining finite search.

EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6.title: Certified Chabauty calculations and Diophantine examples
EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6.summary: Apply quadratic or nonabelian Chabauty with verified rank, height and precision hypotheses. Compare the resulting p-adic candidates with global rational points and work out exhaustive examples for several classes of equations.

EllipticKTheory:E.1.title: Projective elliptic curves and isogenies
EllipticKTheory:E.1.summary: Construct the smooth projective scheme of a nonsingular Weierstrass curve and compare its rational points and group law with the equation-based description. Relate isogenies, divisors, kernels and invariant differentials across these descriptions.

EllipticKTheory:E.5.title: Pullback, transfer and the K-theory projection formula
EllipticKTheory:E.5.summary: Construct K-theory pullbacks and appropriate proper pushforwards for curves. For finite flat maps and isogenies, prove the projection formula using the K₀ class of the direct-image algebra, simplifying to degree multiplication only when justified.

EllipticKTheory:E.8.title: Elliptic K-groups, symbols and integral residues
EllipticKTheory:E.8.summary: Relate K₀ through K₃ of elliptic curves to localization, coniveau and arithmetic-integral symbols. Work out nontrivial symbol classes, non-rational closed-point residues and bad-fibre integrality calculations without asserting a general explicit classification of all groups.

EllipticRegulators:ER.6.title: Integral elliptic regulators and Beilinson’s conjecture
EllipticRegulators:ER.6.summary: Formulate the elliptic Beilinson conjecture on the integral part of K-theory using its determinant line and normalized L-value. Distinguish a constructed nonzero regulator class from a theorem describing the entire regulator space.

EllipticRegulators:ER.8.title: Syntomic elliptic regulators at good reduction
EllipticRegulators:ER.8.summary: Compare syntomic regulators with explicit symbols and p-adic elliptic integrals in good-reduction cases. Formulate the associated p-adic Beilinson conjecture with its periods and exceptional factors, separate from the proved real-regulator identities.

EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceCompari.title: Perverse sheaves and decomposition in endoscopy
EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceCompari.summary: Use scheme-theoretic duality and perverse sheaves to study the geometric correspondences occurring in endoscopy. Separate the construction of the perverse category from later purity and decomposition results.

EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceCompari.title: Verdier duality and perverse intermediate extension
EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceCompari.summary: Develop the duality, middle-perverse truncation, recollement and intermediate-extension statements required for endoscopic geometry. These constructions precede the pure decomposition theorem.

EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceCompari.title: Pure intersection complexes and decomposition
EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceCompari.summary: Apply the pure intersection-complex and decomposition results needed in the geometric proof of endoscopic transfer. Preserve the coefficient, weight and properness assumptions of those theorems.

EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceCompari.title: Unitary base change and Igusa cohomology comparison
EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceCompari.summary: Compare unitary automorphic characters with general linear groups through the specified base-change identities. Relate these identities to the separate Igusa-cohomology comparison, retaining split-place and coefficient hypotheses.

EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E0.title: Quasicategories, differential graded nerves and derived sheaves
EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E0.summary: Construct mapping spaces, functors, equivalences and coherent limits in a model of higher categories. Build the differential graded nerve of complexes and identify its mapping spaces and homotopy category.

EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5.title: Monoidal stable categories and animated algebra
EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5.summary: Construct symmetric monoidal stable higher categories, operadic algebras, modules and Ind-completions. Develop the animated commutative algebra and coherent group actions needed for geometric and cohomological constructions.

EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract.title: Symmetric monoidal stable categories
EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract.summary: Construct symmetric monoidal higher categories and their algebras, modules and functors with coherent universal properties. Develop exact and idempotent-complete stable categories and Karoubi completion.

EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:cotangent-expo.title: Cotangent complexes and derived algebra comparisons
EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:cotangent-expo.summary: Relate cotangent complexes to derivations, transitivity and base change, with derived exterior powers and Tor-amplitude conditions. Compare animated commutative algebra with other derived-algebra models only in the valid characteristic-dependent ranges.

EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:spectra-compar.title: Spectra and Eilenberg–Mac Lane comparison
EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:spectra-compar.summary: Compare concrete spectra and spectral modules with the abstract monoidal stable-category construction. Prove the tensor, Eilenberg–Mac Lane and coherent group-action comparisons used in derived sheaf theory.

EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.0.title: Constructible coefficients and cohomology with supports
EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.0.summary: Construct cohomology with supports as a localization fibre, retaining the closed immersion and coefficient complexes. Compare coefficient extension and reduction, derived tensors, compact-support projection formulas and Künneth maps.

EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.5.title: Perverse sheaves and intermediate extension
EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.5.summary: Construct the middle perverse t-structure on the appropriate constructible category of a finite-type scheme over a field. Prove truncation, recollement and intermediate extension, including the characterization by absence of boundary subobjects and quotients.

EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.8.title: Cohomological correspondences and Frobenius duality
EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.8.summary: Construct cohomological correspondences and fixed-point trace classes using Verdier duality. Relate Frobenius characteristic polynomials in complementary degrees through Poincaré pairings, with the required properness and trace hypotheses.

EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems:ES.0.title: Selmer conditions, quotients and core rank
EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems:ES.0.summary: Construct local Selmer conditions and propagate them through lattice quotients and rationalization. Relate annihilators under local duality, cartesian conditions and core rank using finite-level Euler-characteristic formulas.

EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems:ES.8.title: Iwasawa specialization of Euler systems
EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems:ES.8.summary: Construct inverse-limit systems and specialize Euler and Kolyvagin classes under explicit control hypotheses. Distinguish residual primitivity from Iwasawa primitivity and track exceptional primes and finite or pseudo-null error terms.

EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3.title: Cyclotomic main-conjecture equality
EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture:L3.summary: Use cyclotomic-unit index and class-number formulas to turn characteristic-ideal divisibilities into equalities. Treat character components and augmentation factors separately and retain finite-level errors before passing to the tower.

ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES0:.title: Excursion operators and the Bernstein center
ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES0:.summary: Compare the center arising from excursion operators with the classical Bernstein-block description over characteristic-zero coefficients. Keep this comparison separate from the operator construction over more general coefficient rings.

ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES4.title: Spectral support and localization
ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES4.summary: Define support through central functions on the relevant pieces of the Langlands-parameter space. Study localization, exact triangles, coefficient change and duality, with applications to commuting actions on local shtuka cohomology.

ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES6:.title: Contragredients and the Chevalley involution
ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES6:.summary: Relate Bernstein–Zelevinsky duality and smooth contragredients to the Chevalley involution on Langlands parameters. Retain the induction and duality hypotheses needed beyond supercuspidal representations.

ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod:ES.4.title: Minor arcs, Waring’s problem and sums of primes
ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod:ES.4.summary: Combine major- and minor-arc estimates to prove specified Waring-type, prime-sum and many-variable results. Prime-weighted problems require their own decomposition identities and bilinear estimates, with explicit variable and degree ranges.

ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod:ES.5.title: Uniform bounds for rational and integral points
ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod:ES.5.summary: Compare determinant-method and arithmetic-geometric counting arguments. State bounds with explicit dependence on degree, coefficients and height, keeping upper bounds distinct from positive asymptotic main terms.

FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems:R28.title: Tate modules, Hom groups and rational isogenies
FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems:R28.summary: Apply semisimplicity and the Tate-module description of homomorphisms to detect isogenies and prove finiteness within rational isogeny classes. Derive the required rank-one Hom and prime-degree isogeny consequences for elliptic curves.

FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F0.title: The adic Fargues–Fontaine curve
FarguesFontaineDiamonds:F0.summary: Describe the punctured Witt-vector space attached to a characteristic-p perfectoid field and its Frobenius quotient. Use its rational annuli and adic topology as the geometric starting point for diamond comparison.

FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums:FF.5.title: Character-sum bounds and local arithmetic
FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums:FF.5.summary: Apply character-sum estimates and finite-ring calculations to exponential sums, local densities and exact arithmetic algorithms. Keep the conductor and degree constants explicit in each specialization.

FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.0.title: Source versions and declaration audit
FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.0.summary: Administrative record of source versions, imports and theorem assumptions. This task checks which results can be reused; it introduces no mathematical theorem.

FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.5.title: Compilation and proof-assumption checks
FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.5.summary: Administrative checks for compilation, proof-task tracking and theorem assumptions. This task validates integration of mathematical results without defining an additional mathematical topic.

FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.7.title: Divisor arithmetic and explicit function-field computations
FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.7.summary: Compute divisors, ray characters, conductors and L-polynomials with exact finite-field and Riemann–Roch methods. Relate global function fields to local completions at a chosen place.

GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer.title: Soluble residual modularity in characteristic two
GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer.summary: Construct modularity witnesses for the specified characteristic-two representations with soluble projective image. Prove the base-change and descent comparisons needed for compatible systems, retaining ramification and irreducibility conditions.

GL2ModularityLifting:R22.6.title: Dyadic modularity lifting and Barsotti–Tate representations
GL2ModularityLifting:R22.6.summary: Prove the required 2-adic modularity-lifting results and their stronger Barsotti–Tate form. Retain residual-image, real-place and local-deformation hypotheses through the twisting arguments.

GL2ModularityLifting:R32.1.title: Modularity-lifting theorems across residual characteristics
GL2ModularityLifting:R32.1.summary: State separate lifting results for odd-prime residually modular, dyadic nonsolvable, residually reducible and ordinary characteristic-three cases. Compare residual-image formulations with their exact local exceptions.

GL2ModularityLifting:R32.5.title: Ordinary modularity lifting at p = 3
GL2ModularityLifting:R32.5.summary: Use ordinary lifting and the appropriate crystalline calculation to treat the characteristic-three branch. Match the residual characters and twisting normalization rather than applying a theorem restricted to larger primes.

GL2ModularityLifting:R32.6.title: Modularity across changes of coefficient prime
GL2ModularityLifting:R32.6.summary: Transfer modularity through compatible systems while changing coefficient prime. Treat reducible reductions at ramified primes separately, using de Rham lifting under the available local-comparison hypotheses.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.2.title: Ring K-theory and the plus construction
GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.2.summary: Construct K-theory from finitely generated projective modules and compare the Q-construction with direct-sum group completion. Identify the zero component with the plus construction on the stable general linear group.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.2:plus.title: Ring K-theory and the plus construction
GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.2:plus.summary: Construct K-theory from finitely generated projective modules and compare the Q-construction with direct-sum group completion. Identify the zero component with the plus construction on the stable general linear group.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.2:low-degree-c.title: Low-degree comparisons in ring K-theory
GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.2:low-degree-c.summary: Compare the homotopy groups of ring K-theory with the explicit low-degree constructions. Preserve the natural maps between the Q-construction, stable general linear groups and their plus constructions.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.4.title: Waldhausen’s S-construction and delooping
GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.4.summary: Construct the simplicial categories of filtered objects in a Waldhausen category and iterate them to form K-theory spectra. Prove additivity, delooping and the relevant fibration and comparison theorems with their hypotheses.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.4:construction.title: Waldhausen’s S-construction and delooping
GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.4:construction.summary: Construct the simplicial categories of filtered objects in a Waldhausen category and iterate them to form K-theory spectra. Prove additivity, delooping and the relevant fibration and comparison theorems with their hypotheses.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.7.title: Morita invariance and products in K-theory
GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.7.summary: Prove invariance under the relevant categorical equivalences and compatibility with products and filtered colimits. Construct external products and relate them to localization boundaries, transfers, K₀ tensor products and K₁ units.

FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.1.summary: Develop the localization, integral closure, tensor-product and completion constructions used in arithmetic geometry. FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.2.summary: Relate Haar and product measures, Lebesgue and Bochner integration, Fourier and Mellin transforms, and holomorphic continuation.
