FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.3.title: Homological algebra and sheaves
FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.3.summary: Develop limits, adjunctions, abelian and exact categories, resolutions, derived functors and spectral sequences. Relate monoidal structures and sheafification through natural comparison maps, distinguishing ordinary derived categories from their higher-categorical enhancements.

FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.4.title: Local and global arithmetic foundations
FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.4.summary: Relate number fields, local fields, ramification and class field theory through norms, reciprocity and Frobenius. Connect profinite cohomology, Chebotarev, modular forms and elliptic curves using compatible arithmetic conventions.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups#l.title: Pinned Chevalley–Demazure group schemes
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups#l.summary: Construct split reductive group schemes over the integers from root data, equipped with a maximal torus, Borel subgroup and chosen simple-root vectors. Prove base-change compatibility, root-subgroup relations and uniqueness of pinned isomorphisms, with the exceptional small-characteristic isogenies.

GeneralizedHeegnerCycles:GH.6.title: Nonvanishing and Selmer ranks for Heegner cycles
GeneralizedHeegnerCycles:GH.6.summary: Study nonvanishing of generalized Heegner cycles and its consequences for Selmer groups, with the conductor, root-number and residual-representation hypotheses made explicit. Relate rank-one universal norms and nonzero cycle classes to rank and parity statements without assuming a height formula from an analytic zero alone.

GeneralizedHeegnerCycles:GH.8.title: Weight-two specialization and Iwasawa comparisons
GeneralizedHeegnerCycles:GH.8.summary: Compare generalized Heegner cycles in weight two with Heegner points, tracking parametrizations, differentials, twists and periods. Relate ordinary-family reciprocity laws to characteristic ideals and determinant normalizations in Iwasawa theory.

GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS0:Schubert-sm.title: Schubert cells and cohomological smoothness
GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS0:Schubert-sm.summary: Describe Schubert cells using truncated positive loop groups, flag varieties and unipotent fibers. Establish their cohomological smoothness away from the residue characteristic, with the expected root-theoretic dimension and Galois descent.

GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS4:rational-re.title: Rational Satake semisimplicity and reductivity
GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS4:rational-re.summary: Use proper finite-type models of Witt-vector Schubert varieties and the decomposition theorem to prove semisimplicity of the rational Satake category. Deduce reductivity of its generic Tannakian group; integral and modular coefficients require separate arguments.

GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:.title: Lattice reduction, heights and counting
GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:.summary: Develop lattice reduction with exact changes of basis and quantitative approximation bounds. Apply the resulting reduced bases to height estimates and arithmetic counting problems.

GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.6.title: Global-to-local deformation presentations
GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.6.summary: Describe global Galois deformation rings by their maps to local deformation rings, including dimensions, universal representations and auxiliary-prime conditions. Track compatibility with prescribed local behavior and real places at the prime two.

GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.0.title: Periods, heights and normalizations
GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.0.summary: Compare the normalizations of automorphic L-functions, complex multiplication traces, reciprocity maps and arithmetic heights. Calculate how changes in differentials, polarizations, measures and periods rescale height pairings and their determinants.

HabiroCohomologyFoundations:HQ.7.title: Explicit Habiro cohomology and specialization
HabiroCohomologyFoundations:HQ.7.summary: Calculate polynomial q-differentials, finite étale arithmetic examples and specializations at q = 1. Compare these calculations with de Rham and p-adic cohomology, distinguishing Hodge completion from the uncompleted theory and accounting for derived-limit and torsion terms.

HabiroCyclotomicCompletions:HC.6.title: Taylor evaluation and cyclotomic substitution
HabiroCyclotomicCompletions:HC.6.summary: Construct Taylor expansion, evaluation and p-adic substitution maps for cyclotomic completions and their modules. Work out examples over the integers and at a primitive third root of unity, retaining the hypotheses required for completion and change of cyclotomic order.

HabiroNahmSeries:HB.10.title: Explicit Nahm sums and arithmetic coefficients
HabiroNahmSeries:HB.10.summary: Study explicit Nahm sums through their algebraic solutions, Bloch and K-theory classes, excluded primes and coefficient modules. Include rank-one product identities and q-difference equations, while treating topological invariance as a separate mathematical question.

HabiroNumberFields:HB.1.title: Integral Bloch groups and finite Chern classes
HabiroNumberFields:HB.1.summary: Compare integral definitions of Bloch groups, keeping track of the torsion differences at two and three. Construct finite Chern classes from K₃ using Bockstein maps, Tate twists and Galois cohomology, with the relevant roots-of-unity and ramification hypotheses.

HabiroRings:HR.6.title: Habiro rings as degree-zero cohomology
HabiroRings:HR.6.summary: Identify relative Habiro rings with degree-zero étale q-Hodge and Habiro cohomology. Compare multiplication, cyclotomic specialization and completion at q = 1, together with scalar and Picard-group constructions for modules indexed by K₃.

HabiroRings:HR.7.title: Arithmetic and toric Habiro examples
HabiroRings:HR.7.summary: Calculate Habiro rings over the integers, finite étale arithmetic rings and toric bases, including the effect of inverting primes. Distinguish evaluation at a root of unity from its full Taylor expansion, and compare q-Witt Frobenius transitions with degree-zero cohomology.

HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas:HS4.title: Fusion, duality and Weil actions
HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas:HS4.summary: Establish compatibility of Hecke kernels with permutations, fusion and iterated modifications. Construct creation and annihilation of dual legs through evaluation and coevaluation, and prove compatibility with Weil-group actions.

HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.5.title: Local reciprocity at Kolyvagin primes
HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.5.summary: Prove the finite–singular relations at Kolyvagin primes and compare transverse, self-dual and cartesian local conditions. Construct auxiliary primes by Chebotarev and account for errors arising at the coefficient prime and from Tamagawa factors.

HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.7s.title: Exceptional primes and complex multiplication
HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.7s.summary: Study the exceptional-prime and complex-multiplication branches of Heegner-point descent, including Kolyvagin error bounds and real-multiplication methods. The intended all-prime conclusions require separate dyadic and complex-multiplication arguments beyond the generic-prime case.

HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.8c.title: Anticyclotomic nonvanishing hypotheses
HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.8c.summary: Study non-torsion of Heegner-point traces in anticyclotomic towers and the more general totally real and complex-multiplication setting. Keep track of conductor, central-character and root-number conditions, distinguishing existence at some conductor from nonvanishing for every character.

HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheo.title: Higher reciprocity and arithmetic surfaces
HigherLocalFieldsAndHigherClassFieldTheo.summary: Apply residue and reciprocity maps to Brauer groups and duality in Galois cohomology. Work out two-dimensional local-field and arithmetic-surface examples, with norm compatibility and the required coefficient restrictions.

HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:.title: Classical modular curves and Hilbert geometry
HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:.summary: Recover classical modular curves from the degree-one Hilbert modular setting and compare the geometry over real quadratic fields. Study dimensions, rational boundary components, connected components, descent and the constraints on weights imposed by central units.

IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.title: Generic Hecke localization and cohomological concentration
IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.summary: Study cohomology localized at a Hecke ideal under genericity conditions on the residual Galois representation and Frobenius eigenvalues. Relate the surviving ordinary strata to vanishing below the middle dimension, and compactly supported vanishing above it.

InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGro.title: Explicit Galois realizations and dessins
InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGro.summary: Construct explicit field extensions and covers with prescribed Galois groups, and analyze specialization. Study Belyi pairs and dessins, their Galois action and peripheral inertia, distinguishing fields of moduli from fields of definition.

K3BlochGroups:V.1.title: K₃ and the homology of the Steinberg group
K3BlochGroups:V.1.summary: Relate K₃ to the third integral homology of the stable Steinberg group using its superperfectness and the Hurewicz theorem. Develop explicit bar cycles, boundaries and stabilization maps for arithmetic calculations.

K3BlochGroups:V.3.title: The pre-Bloch group and five-term relations
K3BlochGroups:V.3.summary: Construct the pre-Bloch group from five-term relations and define the Bloch group as the kernel of its tensor-valued boundary. Compare integral conventions carefully, since antisymmetric tensor quotients and exterior squares differ by torsion.

KTheoryLowDegrees:U.6.title: K₁, determinants and the plus construction
KTheoryLowDegrees:U.6.summary: Identify K₁ with the fundamental group of the plus construction and compare determinants and transfer maps. Calculate examples for the integers, finite fields, localizations and products, using explicit matrix identities.

KTheoryLowDegrees:Z.2.title: Rank functions on the prime spectrum
KTheoryLowDegrees:Z.2.summary: Define the rank of a finite projective module as a locally constant function on the prime spectrum. Derive the field and local-ring cases and explain why disconnected rings require separate ranks on their connected components.

KTheoryLowDegrees:Z.6.title: K₀, Euler classes and projective bundles
KTheoryLowDegrees:Z.6.summary: Compare the Grothendieck group of projective modules with degree-zero algebraic K-theory. Study Euler classes, localization and Cartan maps, and calculate projective-line and Dedekind-domain examples that distinguish rank from the ideal class.

LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.0.title: Nearby cycles, inertia and vanishing cycles
LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.0.summary: Construct nearby cycles over a henselian trait, with inertia actions and Milnor-fiber stalk descriptions. Define vanishing cycles by the specialization triangle and prove the relevant proper-pushforward and smooth-base-change comparisons.

LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.6.title: Perverse nearby cycles and intermediate extension
LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.6.summary: Establish exactness of nearby and vanishing cycles for the perverse t-structure, with the shifts appropriate to a map to the affine line. Compare intermediate extension, duality and adic realization across the permitted coefficient systems.

LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.5.title: Dyadic and boundary-weight deformation rings
LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.5.summary: Study Galois deformation conditions at the prime two and at weights outside the basic Fontaine–Laffaille range. Include crystalline and Barsotti–Tate conditions, twists and real-place behavior without relying on trace decompositions that fail in characteristic two.

LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6.title: Dimensions and components of local deformation rings
LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.6.summary: Describe local Galois deformation rings with prescribed conditions through their dimensions, tangent spaces, components and nonemptiness. Include good-dihedral conditions and dyadic weight-two types needed to compare local and global deformations.

LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory:LD.5.title: Definable counting and local densities
LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory:LD.5.summary: Apply definability and transfer principles to arithmetic counting and local densities. Specify the language, parameters and finite sets of exceptional primes needed for uniform statements.

MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.6.title: Factorization of theta integrals and seesaw identities
MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.6.summary: Factor global theta integrals into local expressions with compatible self-dual measures. Establish spectral projections and seesaw identities in their convergent or regularized settings, keeping these comparisons distinct from a complete global period formula.

ModularCurvesPartII:R12.6.title: Descent, diamond operators and connected components
ModularCurvesPartII:R12.6.summary: Study descent of modular curves across levels and compare diamond operators, complex conjugation and rational cusp fields. Relate analytic connected components to their algebraic counterparts.

ModularCurvesPartII:R13.6.title: Degeneration of modular curves at bad primes
ModularCurvesPartII:R13.6.summary: Describe dual graphs, component maps and formal parameters at cusps in degenerating modular curves. Compare Hecke and degeneracy maps on bad fibers and their nearby-cycle descriptions.

ModularCurvesPartII:R14.4.title: Ihara’s lemma and level-change maps
ModularCurvesPartII:R14.4.summary: Study Ihara’s lemma and the injectivity and torsion properties of maps between modular-curve cohomology at different levels. Track the Hecke actions and local hypotheses required for level change.

ModularCurvesPartII:R14.6.title: Monodromy, Hecke operators and modular Jacobians
ModularCurvesPartII:R14.6.summary: Study character groups and monodromy exact sequences with their Hecke actions, including the Eichler–Shimura relation on special fibers. Compare freeness under auxiliary level change and Abel–Jacobi maps normalized at a rational cusp.

ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L5.title: Euler factors, coefficient changes and μ-invariants
ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L5.summary: Compare Iwasawa-theoretic statements under changes of coefficients and Euler factors, and study their consequences for μ-invariants. Separate ordinary higher-weight and crystalline nonordinary settings, with conjectural extensions stated under their own hypotheses.

ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L6.title: Comparing branches of modular Iwasawa theory
ModularIwasawaMainConjectures:L6.summary: Compare Selmer groups, determinant lines and period normalizations in anticyclotomic, Eisenstein and supersingular settings. Identify the additional reciprocity laws and main-conjecture arguments needed in each branch.

ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L4.title: Weight-two p-adic L-functions and coefficient changes
ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L4.summary: Calculate p-adic L-functions of weight-two forms and their twists in ordinary and supersingular settings. Track refinement choices, Euler factors, scalar extension and the extra restrictions that arise at critical slope.

ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.0.title: Automorphic and Galois normalization
ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.0.summary: Compare automorphic representations and Galois representations through their coefficient fields, infinity types, local parameters and conductors. Fix the reciprocity and twisting conventions needed to state local–global compatibility precisely.

ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.2.title: Potential automorphy and descent
ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.2.summary: Study automorphy after a specified extension of the base field under regularity, polarization, residual-image and local hypotheses. Treat descent back to the original field as a further theorem with its own conditions.

ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.4.title: Classical-group packets and multiplicity formulas
ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.4.summary: Develop the classification of automorphic representations of classical groups through local packets, transfer and global multiplicity formulas. Track the stabilization and fundamental-lemma inputs and distinguish the hypotheses for unitary and symplectic groups.

K2SymbolsBrauer:T.2:graded-map.title: Milnor and algebraic K-theory products
K2SymbolsBrauer:T.2:graded-map.summary: Construct the natural graded map from Milnor K-theory to algebraic K-theory using products. Its degree-two isomorphism is Matsumoto’s theorem; higher degrees require separate comparisons.

K2SymbolsBrauer:T.3:localization-compari.title: Tame symbols and the localization boundary
K2SymbolsBrauer:T.3:localization-compari.summary: Identify the tame symbol of a discrete valuation with the boundary in the algebraic K-theory localization sequence. Develop finite support, higher Milnor residues and transfer formulas with their signs, residue degrees and ramification factors.

LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.7.title: Semistable curves and invariant cycles
LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.7.summary: Compute nearby cycles and monodromy for proper strictly semistable curves from their normalization, nodes and dual graph. Prove invariant-cycle results for the specified smooth-total-space and potentially pure settings, retaining the hypotheses needed for specialization onto inertia invariants.

LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.7.title: Nearby cycles of semistable curves
LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.7.summary: For a proper strictly semistable curve over a henselian trait, calculate nearby cycles, the specialization sequence and monodromy from the normalization and dual graph. Compare this description with component groups, Jacobians and Tate modules.

LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.7.title: Local and global invariant cycles
LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.7.summary: Prove specialization onto inertia invariants for proper families with smooth total space and smooth generic fiber in the stated equicharacteristic setting. Extend the argument to potentially pure complexes and global invariant cycles under the required arithmetic-model and support hypotheses.

MotivicEtaleKTheory:M.6a.title: Coniveau filtrations and cycle complexes
MotivicEtaleKTheory:M.6a.summary: Construct the support filtration and homotopy-coniveau tower of algebraic K-theory. Use moving and excision to identify its layers with cycle complexes for the specified smooth schemes and compare the resulting global models.

NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties.title: Monodromy and reduction of abelian varieties
NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties.summary: Construct character-group exact sequences and monodromy maps compatible with degeneracy maps. Study semistable and good reduction, and compare equation-level elliptic invariants with their scheme-theoretic definitions.

NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa:NE.5.title: Noncommutative zeta elements and interpolation
NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa:NE.5.summary: Formulate zeta elements in localized K₁ through their localization boundary and interpolation at Artin representations. Track periods, local factors and exceptional zeros, and compare norm, restriction and abelianization with commutative determinant formulas.

NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa:NE.6.title: Noncommutative Iwasawa main theorems
NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa:NE.6.summary: Develop the integral logarithms, congruences, abelian pseudomeasures and localization calculations used in noncommutative Iwasawa main theorems. State existence and uniqueness separately, preserving the odd-prime, totally real, admissibility and μ-invariant assumptions of each result.

NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa:NE.7.title: Leading terms and equivariant descent
NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa:NE.7.summary: Construct leading terms through derived specialization, Bockstein maps and regulators when ordinary evaluations vanish. Prove descent in relative K-theory under the required semisimplicity and finiteness conditions, including exceptional zeros and noncommutative Fitting invariants.

OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLif.title: Ordinary modularity lifting and classical families
OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLif.summary: State ordinary modularity-lifting results with their finite-level automorphic realizations and precise local hypotheses. Construct the classical ordinary families that connect these lifting results to subsequent p-adic variation.

OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O8.title: Siegel and unitary overconvergent coefficients
OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O8.summary: Construct overconvergent coefficient sheaves on Siegel varieties over the established anticanonical domains. Compare scalar and vector-valued algebraic specializations with Hodge bundles, and extend the coefficient construction to unitary domains when their analytic reduction is supplied.

PELModuli:M5.title: Siegel, Hilbert and unitary moduli problems
PELModuli:M5.summary: Construct Siegel moduli in every dimension, Hilbert moduli from trace pairings over totally real fields, and unitary examples with specified signatures. Calculate reflex fields and dimensions and include nonprincipal polarization types.

PELModuli:M6.title: Arithmetic moduli, level structures and descent
PELModuli:M6.summary: Construct moduli stacks at arbitrary level and universal abelian schemes at levels where the moduli problem is rigidified. Compare rational moduli points with families by calculating the descent obstruction, including examples with nonprincipal polarizations.

PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomo.title: Rigid, crystalline and étale Frobenius comparisons
PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomo.summary: For smooth proper varieties over finite fields, compare rational rigid and crystalline cohomology compatibly with Frobenius. Combine these comparisons with purity and finite-extension zeta identities to identify the individual Frobenius characteristic polynomials with their étale counterparts.

PadicHodgeRegulators:D.5.title: Syntomic regulators of curves
PadicHodgeRegulators:D.5.summary: Construct degree-two syntomic regulators for smooth proper curves under the specified good-reduction hypotheses and compare them with explicit symbol formulas. Prove pullback, pushforward and specialization formulas, separating the additional logarithmic theory required for semistable reduction.

PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations.title: Robba rings and analytic coefficients
PadicHodgeTheory:P7:annulus-foundations.summary: Construct bounded, overconvergent and Robba rings from convergent Laurent series on annuli, with their norms, topologies, Frobenius and cyclotomic actions. Prove the restriction, coefficient-extension and completed-tensor comparisons needed for p-adic representations.

PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4.title: Integral p-adic Hodge theory in small weights
PadicHodgeTheory:R06.4.summary: Compare integral classifications with their rational period-functor consequences in the Fontaine–Laffaille range. Retain the weight intervals and nilpotence restrictions at boundary weights, and treat the prime two and Breuil–Kisin cases separately.

PerfectoidShimuraVarieties:S0.general.title: Infinite-level diamonds for general Shimura data
PerfectoidShimuraVarieties:S0.general.summary: Construct the infinite-level diamond as the limit of finite-level canonical models for general Shimura data. Perfectoid representability and Hodge–Tate period maps require further geometric results.

PerfectoidSpaces:P0.title: Almost rings and almost modules
PerfectoidSpaces:P0.summary: Develop almost mathematics relative to an idempotent ideal satisfying the required flatness conditions. Construct almost-zero modules, almostification, tensor and Hom, and almost finite étale algebras, then compare the resulting categories for the standard perfectoid ideals.

PeriodsAndSpecialValues:PS.6.title: Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer and Bloch–Kato formulas
PeriodsAndSpecialValues:PS.6.summary: Identify the terms of motivic determinant lines with Mordell–Weil regulators, torsion, periods, Tamagawa numbers and Tate–Shafarevich groups in the established cases. Distinguish rank and finiteness results from fixed-prime valuations and complete leading-coefficient formulas.

PeriodsAndSpecialValues:PS.7.title: Rigorous computation of periods and special values
PeriodsAndSpecialValues:PS.7.summary: Calculate exact algebraic factors and rigorously bounded approximations to period integrals and convergent L-value expressions. Compare normalizations and prove error bounds sufficient for stated inequalities, while retaining higher-rank and general special-value formulas as conjectures where unresolved.

Polylogarithms:P.6.title: Leopoldt’s conjecture and polylogarithmic identities
Polylogarithms:P.6.summary: Formulate Leopoldt’s conjecture as injectivity of the completed global-unit map to local logarithms and prove its equivalence with nonvanishing of the p-adic regulator after removing torsion. Establish explicit five-term, conjugation and differential identities for low-weight polylogarithms.

PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure:PA.0.title: Integral cohomology and Hecke actions
PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure:PA.0.summary: Compare algebraic local systems and finite-level cohomology complexes with their integral Hecke actions. Prove compatibility with coefficient change, level change and boundary localization, and construct the boundary filtrations and splittings under their stated genericity hypotheses.

PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure:PA.5.title: Operations on compatible Galois systems
PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure:PA.5.summary: Study restriction, tensor products, duals, character twists and symmetric powers of compatible systems of Galois representations. Track Frobenius polynomials, Hodge–Tate weights, monodromy and lattices, asserting regularity, purity and polarization only under the hypotheses that preserve them.

PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:.title: Residual and characteristic-zero potential modularity
PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:.summary: Distinguish potential modularity of a residual representation from potential modularity of a supplied characteristic-zero lift. State the field extensions and local hypotheses in each case and compare their consequences for modular deformation problems and compatible systems.

PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:.title: Modularity lifting in the Khare–Wintenberger range
PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:.summary: Establish modularity lifting for crystalline and semistable weight-two representations and the specified odd-prime weight intervals. Retain cyclotomic irreducibility at odd primes and the nonsolvable-image and residual-weight restrictions in dyadic cases.

PrismaticCohomology:PR.5.title: Absolute prismatic cohomology and Cartier–Witt stacks
PrismaticCohomology:PR.5.summary: Construct absolute prismatic sites and Cartier–Witt stacks and compare their crystals with relative prismatic cohomology. Develop Frobenius, Nygaard filtrations, Breuil–Kisin twists and syntomic complexes under the required boundedness and completeness assumptions.

RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.0.title: Elliptic L-functions, analytic rank and twists
RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.0.summary: Construct the analytic continuation and functional equation of an elliptic curve’s Euler product through modularity. Define analytic rank by its finite vanishing order at the central point, prove root-number parity, and compare quadratic twists through every local Euler factor.

RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.9.title: Explicit rank-zero and rank-one BSD comparisons
RankZeroOneBSD:BSD.9.summary: Distinguish analytic-rank equality, finiteness of the Tate–Shafarevich group and fixed-prime or all-prime leading-term formulas. Work out elliptic-curve examples with rigorously bounded central values or derivatives, tracking height and period normalizations and the arithmetic hypotheses of each conclusion.

RefinedTraceMethods:RT.4.title: Complex K-theory and q-Hodge comparisons
RefinedTraceMethods:RT.4.summary: Construct connective and periodic complex K-theory from vector bundles and Bott periodicity. Study their trace-theoretic filtrations and comparisons with q-Hodge and Habiro cohomology under the required spherical-lift and coefficient hypotheses.

RefinedTraceMethods:RT.4:topological.title: Complex K-theory and Bott periodicity
RefinedTraceMethods:RT.4:topological.summary: Construct complex topological K-theory from vector bundles and prove Bott periodicity with its multiplicative structure. Identify the homotopy groups of its connective and periodic spectra and prove that inverting the Bott element relates them.

RefinedTraceMethods:RT.4:q-Hodge.title: Even filtrations and q-Hodge cohomology
RefinedTraceMethods:RT.4:q-Hodge.summary: For a quasisyntomic ring with two invertible and a specified connective spherical E₂-lift, construct a complete multiplicative even filtration with graded q-de Rham and q-Hodge comparisons. Develop genuine finite-cyclic fixed-point constructions and their compatibility with Bott localization.

RefinedTraceMethods:RT.4:Habiro-comparis.title: Trace-theoretic Habiro cohomology
RefinedTraceMethods:RT.4:Habiro-comparis.summary: Compare even-graded Habiro cohomology with limits of finite-cyclic and residual-circle fixed-point constructions in periodic complex K-theory. For number fields, retain the specified spherical étale lift and the inversion of primes dividing six and the discriminant.

RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6.title: Quasisyntomic traces and prismatic filtrations
RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6.summary: Compute topological Hochschild and cyclic invariants by quasisyntomic descent and construct their complete multiplicative filtrations. Compare the graded pieces with prismatic cohomology, Nygaard filtrations, Breuil–Kisin twists and syntomic complexes, including the trace-theoretic instances used in Habiro cohomology.

SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.6.title: Cycle classes and arithmetic cohomology comparisons
SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.6.summary: Construct natural comparisons among crystalline, prismatic, analytic and adic cohomology under their precise geometric and coefficient hypotheses. Compare cycle classes, traces and intersection pairings through these maps.

SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation:R20.6.title: Bounded level and weight-two modular forms
SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation:R20.6.summary: Derive bounded-level, weight-two and trivial-character modular realizations for the relevant elliptic representations at sufficiently large good primes. Track the optimization hypotheses and the additional dyadic arguments required for the full strong form of Serre’s conjecture.

ShimuraCompactifications:C2.general.title: Toroidal compactifications for general Shimura data
ShimuraCompactifications:C2.general.summary: Glue and descend toroidal compactifications using canonical models for general Shimura data. Preserve the rational boundary components, cone data and cusp stabilizers throughout the construction.

ShimuraCompactifications:C3.general.title: Hecke maps on general toroidal compactifications
ShimuraCompactifications:C3.general.summary: Extend level-change, cone-refinement and Hecke maps to toroidal compactifications for general Shimura data. Prove compatibility with boundary descriptions without asserting integral models at all primes.

ShimuraVarieties:V8.general.title: Functoriality of general canonical models
ShimuraVarieties:V8.general.summary: Extend level-change and functorial comparison maps to canonical models for general Shimura data. Relate these constructions to the previously established Hodge-type and abelian-type cases.

SmallRamificationAndAbelianVarietyBaseCa.title: Small-prime cases of residual modularity
SmallRamificationAndAbelianVarietyBaseCa.summary: Compare the residual modularity cases distinguished by characteristic, weight, ramification and image. Prove the local calculations for exceptional transitions and retain the coefficient assumptions required in each small-prime case.

SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.0.title: The category of smooth representations
SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.0.summary: Construct the abelian category of representations in which every vector has an open stabilizer. Study smooth vectors, compact-open invariants and admissibility, then form the enhanced derived category on this abelian foundation.

SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.0:.title: Smooth representations and compact-open invariants
SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.0:.summary: Construct kernels, cokernels, sums and filtered colimits of smooth representations and the smooth-vector adjunction. Study compact-open invariants and distinguish admissibility from stronger finiteness conditions.

SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.0:.title: The derived category of smooth representations
SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.0:.summary: Construct the enhanced derived category of the abelian category of smooth representations. Relate its objects and derived operations to complexes of representations with open vector stabilizers.

SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.3a.title: Uniform admissibility
SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.3a.summary: For a fixed compact open subgroup, prove a uniform bound on the dimension of its invariants in irreducible smooth complex representations. Derive the bound from Hecke-algebra decompositions, commutative-subalgebra estimates and Burnside’s theorem.

SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.6.title: Integral Hecke finiteness and second adjointness
SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.6.summary: Prove finiteness over a finitely generated center for the specified Hecke algebras over noetherian ℓ-adic coefficient algebras, with ℓ different from the residue characteristic. Establish second adjointness when the residue characteristic is invertible, tracking modulus characters and normalization choices.

SpecialValuesBirchTate:B.1.title: The Birch–Tate formula
SpecialValuesBirchTate:B.1.summary: For a totally real number field, formulate the value of its Dedekind zeta function at −1 in terms of the order of K₂ of its integers and the invariants of the second Tate twist. Establish the finiteness of these arithmetic terms and retain the degree-dependent sign.

SpecialValuesBirchTate:B.3.title: Birch–Tate over the rationals and quadratic fields
SpecialValuesBirchTate:B.3.summary: Derive the Birch–Tate formula over the rationals from independent calculations of K₂ of the integers, the second Tate-twist invariants and the zeta value at −1. Study real quadratic examples through tame kernels, cyclotomic computations and Dirichlet L-functions.

SpecialValuesBirchTate:B.8.title: Higher Lichtenbaum formulas and regulators
SpecialValuesBirchTate:B.8.summary: Formulate higher special-value formulas using algebraic K-groups, regulators and determinant lines. Prove the specified odd-primary consequences for totally real fields, treat real-place and dyadic corrections separately, and include leading terms when complex places force vanishing.

StableHomotopyKTheory:H.5.title: Spectra, stable homotopy and deloopings
StableHomotopyKTheory:H.5.summary: Construct spectra, stable homotopy groups, fiber and cofiber sequences and the stable homotopy category. Prove the delooping comparison for the iterated S-construction and construct the products needed for graded algebraic K-theory.

StableHomotopyKTheory:H.5:spectra.title: Spectra and stable homotopy
StableHomotopyKTheory:H.5:spectra.summary: Construct suspension spectra, loops, shifts and stable homotopy groups indexed by integers. Develop stable equivalences, fiber and cofiber sequences, their long exact sequences and the stable homotopy category.

StableHomotopyKTheory:H.5:S-delooping.title: The S-construction and K-theory spectra
StableHomotopyKTheory:H.5:S-delooping.summary: Prove that iterating the S-construction gives a connective spectrum through its delooping theorem. Construct smash products and the induced pairings on homotopy groups, with the coherent multiplicative refinements required for K-theory.

TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure:TC.4.title: Torsion cohomology and Hecke polynomials
TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure:TC.4.summary: Compare the constructions taking finite-level torsion cohomology to Hecke characteristic polynomials after the specified nilpotent quotient. Prove compatibility across coefficient powers and levels, including class-field and modular-curve examples where torsion classes need not lift to characteristic zero.

TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.7.title: Nonarchimedean uniformization and integration
TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.7.summary: Construct Tate uniformization and Schottky quotients for totally degenerate curves, with their period lattices and descent. Compare Coleman primitives, annular residues and global integrals, and relate semistable graph corrections to arithmetic heights.

VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0.title: Isocrystals and Dieudonné–Manin slopes
VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB0.summary: Construct isocrystals as finite-dimensional spaces with an invertible Frobenius-semilinear map. Prove the Dieudonné–Manin classification over the stipulated algebraically closed residue base and calculate simple slopes, morphisms and endomorphism division algebras, including their relation to vector-bundle degrees.

WeightsInEtaleCohomology:R34.6.title: Purity in automorphic Galois representations
WeightsInEtaleCohomology:R34.6.summary: Apply geometric purity to the eigenspaces realizing modular and automorphic Galois representations. Deduce coefficient-independent Frobenius bounds and compatibility with Hecke projectors, using local monodromy–weight results only in the cases where they are established.

WeilConjectures:WC.0.title: Finite-field varieties and geometric Frobenius
WeilConjectures:WC.0.summary: Specify the finite-field varieties, geometric base changes and Frobenius actions underlying zeta functions. Establish finiteness of rational points over finite extensions and keep cohomological degrees and coefficient primes explicit in geometric statements.

WeilConjectures:WC.1.title: Zeta functions and finite extensions
WeilConjectures:WC.1.summary: Relate point counts to numbers of closed points by Möbius inversion and derive the Euler product of the zeta function. Prove compatibility with disjoint unions, open–closed decompositions and finite base extension, and descend cohomological rationality to a normalized rational function over the rationals.

WeilConjectures:WC.6.title: Weights beyond smooth projective varieties
WeilConjectures:WC.6.summary: Extend purity to smooth proper varieties in the permitted setting and use compactly supported cohomology for general finite-type varieties and mixed sheaves. Compare finite-field crystalline and étale Frobenius characteristic polynomials when the required comparison theorem is available.

WeilConjectures:WC.7.title: Zeta functions of projective spaces, curves and products
WeilConjectures:WC.7.summary: Calculate Frobenius factors for projective spaces, finite étale schemes, smooth curves, elliptic curves and products. Relate product varieties through the tensor-product action on cohomology and verify rationality, functional equations and the expected weights in these examples.

Polylogarithms:P.4.title: Polylogarithmic complexes and Zagier’s conjecture
Polylogarithms:P.4.summary: Define rational polylogarithmic complexes using explicit configurations and relations, and construct embedding-wise regulator determinants. Formulate Zagier’s conjecture with its period and discriminant normalization, separating existence of suitable elements, motivic comparison and the special-value identity.

PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra.title: Integral perfectoid rings and their completions
PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra.summary: Construct integral perfectoid rings, their A_inf rings and Fontaine’s θ map, and compare them with Tate perfectoid rings. Distinguish ordinary, derived p-adic and pseudouniformizer-adic completion in passages from semiperfectoid quotients to Tate rings.

ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES7:.title: Division-algebra automorphic forms over function fields
ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES7:.summary: Construct automorphic forms for division algebras over global function fields, including compactness modulo center and discrete spectral decomposition. Establish the simple trace comparisons and prescribed local realizations needed in the stated transfer range, with central-character and auxiliary-place hypotheses retained.

tauceti:Completed/EffectiveBounds#layer-.title: Lattice packing and doubling bounds
tauceti:Completed/EffectiveBounds#layer-.summary: Bound the number of lattice points in boxes and polydiscs using separation and packing arguments. Prove quantitative doubling estimates comparing the points in a region with those in its dilation.

tauceti:Completed/EffectiveBounds#layer-.title: Effective discriminant and ideal-count bounds
tauceti:Completed/EffectiveBounds#layer-.summary: Bound a number-field discriminant using the discriminant of a basis of algebraic integers. Derive explicit upper bounds for the number of nonzero ideals of bounded norm from the Dedekind zeta function, with worked arithmetic examples.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/CombinatorialHeeg.title: Grid homology of knots and links
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/CombinatorialHeeg.summary: Construct knot and link homology from grid diagrams, graded states and counts of empty rectangles. Prove invariance under grid moves, relate the Euler characteristic to the Alexander polynomial and develop concordance bounds, symmetries and filtered refinements.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/CombinatorialHeeg.title: Grid-homology symmetries and genus bounds
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/CombinatorialHeeg.summary: Study symmetries of grid homology and prove that nonzero groups in Alexander grading s give the lower bound g(K) ≥ s for the knot genus. Genus detection requires additional holomorphic theory; the combinatorial result here is the bound.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/CombinatorialHeeg.title: Bigraded modules and filtered chain complexes
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/CombinatorialHeeg.summary: Develop bigraded modules, grading shifts and mapping cones over polynomial rings. Prove the structure theorem for finitely generated bigraded modules over a one-variable polynomial ring and construct filtered chain complexes and filtered chain-homotopy equivalences.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/CombinatorialHeeg.title: Grid diagrams and topological knots
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/CombinatorialHeeg.summary: Relate grid diagrams to knot diagrams, braid closures and embedded knots in the three-sphere. Prove that grid moves generate the equivalence of represented links and compare the grid determinant with the Alexander polynomial.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/CombinatorialHeeg.title: Integral combinatorial Heegaard Floer homology
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/CombinatorialHeeg.summary: Use sign assignments to define combinatorial Heegaard Floer homology over the integers. Develop the twisted refinement for three-manifolds with first Betti number zero, distinguishing invariance under diagram moves from identification with smooth three-manifolds.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ConformalMapping#.title: Local conformal mapping theorems
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ConformalMapping#.summary: Derive Rouché’s theorem, Hurwitz’s theorem and local mapping-degree properties from contour integration and the argument principle. Establish Morera’s theorem and relate locally uniform limits to the geometry of zeros.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Exchangeability#l.title: L² averaging and de Finetti’s theorem
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Exchangeability#l.summary: Use covariance identities and bounds on block averages to study exchangeable and contractable sequences. Develop the L² averaging proof of de Finetti’s theorem for standard-Borel-valued sequences, identifying their conditional independent and identically distributed structure.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Exchangeability#l.title: Equivalent forms of de Finetti’s theorem
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Exchangeability#l.summary: Compare exchangeability, contractability, mixtures of independent identically distributed sequences and conditional independence. Relate empirical measures to the unique mixing law and characterize the extreme exchangeable laws as independent identically distributed laws in the stated setting.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GeometricTopology.title: Manifolds, boundaries and gluing
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GeometricTopology.summary: Construct manifold boundaries, collar and tubular neighborhoods, gluing along boundary faces and connected sums with their choice-independence theorems. Develop piecewise-linear chart structures using locally finite polyhedral subdivisions, while keeping smooth, piecewise-linear and topological structures distinct.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#mil.title: Morse trajectories and Morse homology
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#mil.summary: Construct stable and unstable manifolds and achieve Morse–Smale transversality using Sard’s theorem. Prove compactness and gluing for broken trajectories, define the Morse differential, and identify the resulting invariant homology with singular homology.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#lan.title: Fredholm operators and Sard–Smale transversality
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#lan.summary: Develop Fredholm index theory, stability under compact and small perturbations, and the Fredholm property of strip operators with invertible asymptotics. Prove Sard–Smale transversality and describe regular zero sets of Fredholm sections as manifolds of the expected dimension.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#lan.title: Elliptic theory for Cauchy–Riemann operators
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#lan.summary: Develop Sobolev estimates and regularity for Cauchy–Riemann operators on surfaces and strips, including totally real boundary conditions. Prove Fredholm properties and the boundary Riemann–Roch formula, relating the Maslov index to spectral flow.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#mil.title: Sobolev spaces on surfaces and strips
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#mil.summary: Construct Sobolev spaces of maps on surfaces and strips, their trace maps and multiplication estimates. Retain the condition kp > 2 for the stated multiplication results in dimension two.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#mil.title: Cauchy–Riemann estimates and boundary regularity
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#mil.summary: Prove Calderón–Zygmund estimates for the Cauchy–Riemann operator using the Cauchy kernel and derive interior elliptic regularity. Treat totally real boundary conditions through Schwarz reflection in the specified local setting.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#mil.title: Fredholm index, Maslov index and Riemann–Roch
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#mil.summary: Study linear Cauchy–Riemann operators on disks and strips as Fredholm maps between Sobolev spaces. Prove Riemann–Roch with boundary and relate the index to Maslov indices and spectral flow.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#mil.title: Symplectic structures and pseudoholomorphic maps
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#mil.summary: Define symplectic manifolds, tame and compatible almost complex structures, pseudoholomorphic maps and their energy. Establish the local symplectic geometry supplied by Darboux’s and Moser’s theorems.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#lan.title: Holomorphic Heegaard Floer homology
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#lan.summary: Construct Heegaard Floer homology by counting holomorphic disks in symmetric products of Heegaard surfaces. Develop Spinᶜ structures, Maslov indices and admissibility bounds, prove invariance over the field with two elements, and extend toward integral coefficients and cobordism maps.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#mil.title: Almost complex structures and disk transversality
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#mil.summary: Choose nearly symmetric almost complex structures suitable for Heegaard Floer theory and prove transversality of the relevant holomorphic disks. Use admissibility to obtain the energy bounds needed when monotonicity is unavailable.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#mil.title: Floer variants, cobordisms and surgery triangles
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#mil.summary: Extend Heegaard Floer theory to integral coefficients through orientation systems and construct its plus, minus and infinity variants. Develop holomorphic triangle counts, cobordism maps, surgery exact triangles, correction terms and naturality.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#lan.title: Cylindrical, bordered and knot Floer homology
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#lan.summary: Develop the cylindrical reformulation of Heegaard Floer theory using varying source curves and the appropriate symplectic-field-theory compactness. Extend toward bordered Floer homology and knot Floer homology from doubly pointed diagrams, enabling comparison with grid homology.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/OptimalTransport#.title: Exact finite optimal-transport examples
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/OptimalTransport#.summary: Work out finite, Dirac and product examples across optimal transport and Wasserstein geometry. Compare exact mathematical solutions with numerical approximations whose residuals and error bounds are certified, retaining the hypotheses of the relevant transport and duality theorems.

tauceti:Completed/OrthogonalL2Bases#a1--.title: Hermite polynomials and Gaussian orthogonality
tauceti:Completed/OrthogonalL2Bases#a1--.summary: Prove differentiation, integration-by-parts and generating-function identities for the probabilists’ Hermite polynomials. Establish their Gaussian orthogonality with the exact factorial normalization, in both Lebesgue-density and Gaussian-probability forms.

tauceti:Completed/OrthogonalL2Bases#part.title: Moment determinacy and orthogonal L² bases
tauceti:Completed/OrthogonalL2Bases#part.summary: Derive completeness of weighted polynomial systems from moment determinacy under exponential-integrability hypotheses. Construct normalized Hilbert bases, compare weighted measures through multiplication by the square root of the weight, and prove completeness of product bases for σ-finite measures.

tauceti:Completed/OrthogonalL2Bases#b1--.title: Moment determinacy and completeness
tauceti:Completed/OrthogonalL2Bases#b1--.summary: Prove that an integrable function with sufficient exponential integrability and vanishing polynomial moments is zero almost everywhere, using analyticity and uniqueness of its Fourier transform. Apply this result to completeness of weighted polynomial systems in L², including Gaussian and compactly supported cases.

tauceti:Completed/OrthogonalL2Bases#part.title: Multidimensional Hermite bases
tauceti:Completed/OrthogonalL2Bases#part.summary: Construct multidimensional Hermite bases as products of one-dimensional bases, indexed by multi-indices. Prove completeness for both Lebesgue and Gaussian L² spaces and compare their normalizations through weighting and coordinatewise dilation.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/PDE#lane-a-functi.title: Sobolev and Hölder spaces on domains
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/PDE#lane-a-functi.summary: Construct Sobolev spaces from weak derivatives and compare them with the Bessel-potential scale where they agree. Develop density, embeddings, Poincaré inequalities, traces, extension operators and compactness, together with Hölder spaces for elliptic regularity.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/PDE#milestone-a-3.title: Sobolev and Bessel-potential spaces
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/PDE#milestone-a-3.summary: Prove agreement between integer-order weak-derivative Sobolev spaces and Bessel-potential spaces on Euclidean space. Include the Hilbert-space case and the integer-order comparison for 1 < p < ∞.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/PDE#milestone-b-9.title: Real and complex interpolation
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/PDE#milestone-b-9.summary: Prove the Marcinkiewicz interpolation theorem, deriving strong-type bounds from weak-type estimates. Establish the Riesz–Thorin theorem through complex interpolation of operator norms.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/PDE#milestone-b-1.title: Calderón–Zygmund operators and Fourier multipliers
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/PDE#milestone-b-1.summary: Construct the Calderón–Zygmund decomposition and prove singular-integral bounds on Lᵖ for 1 < p < ∞, with weak type (1,1) and the L∞-to-BMO endpoint. Develop the Mihlin–Hörmander multiplier theorem under its differentiability hypotheses.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/PDE#lane-c-maximu.title: Maximum principles and potential theory
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/PDE#lane-c-maximu.summary: Develop mean-value properties, maximum principles, Hopf’s lemma and Harnack inequalities for harmonic and elliptic equations. Construct fundamental solutions, Green functions and Poisson kernels, and solve Dirichlet problems by Perron’s method with barriers ensuring boundary attainment.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/PDE#lane-d-linear.title: Weak elliptic solutions and the energy method
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/PDE#lane-d-linear.summary: Formulate elliptic boundary-value problems through bounded energy forms and Gårding’s inequality. Use coercivity for existence and uniqueness, compactness for the Fredholm alternative, and a compact self-adjoint inverse to construct the Dirichlet Laplacian’s eigenfunction basis.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/PDE#lane-f-parabo.title: Parabolic equations and heat semigroups
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/PDE#lane-f-parabo.summary: Develop time-dependent Sobolev and Bochner spaces in a Gelfand triple. Prove existence and uniqueness for linear parabolic equations by Galerkin approximation and energy estimates, and construct heat semigroups, their generators and smoothing estimates.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationThe.title: Finite-dimensional representations of sl₂
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationThe.summary: Construct highest-weight modules for sl₂ using raising and lowering operators. Classify finite-dimensional irreducible representations and prove complete reducibility, then deduce integral weights and diagonalizability of the Cartan operator in characteristic zero.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationThe.title: The Jacobson radical and semisimplicity
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationThe.summary: Study the Jacobson radical of a finite-dimensional algebra, its nilpotence and the semisimplicity of the quotient. Prove the radical criterion for semisimplicity and compare radicals and semiprimary structures under passage to the opposite ring.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/UniversalCovers#s.title: Universal covers and deck transformations
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/UniversalCovers#s.summary: Construct the universal cover of a path-connected, locally path-connected and semilocally simply connected space from based paths modulo endpoint-preserving homotopy. Prove the covering and lifting properties and develop the fundamental-group action and deck-transformation group.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/UniversalCovers#s.title: Homotopy groups from universal covers
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/UniversalCovers#s.summary: Use universal covers and deck transformations to calculate the fundamental group of the circle and the vanishing of its higher homotopy groups. Extend these methods to tori, real projective spaces and Eilenberg–Mac Lane spaces.

BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG2.summary: The stack Bun_G parametrizes G-bundles on the relative Fargues–Fontaine curve. Its construction combines v-descent and uniformization by Hecke modifications with the classification of geometric points by B(G); the Kottwitz invariant is locally constant and Newton slopes are semicontinuous. For ℓ ≠ p, the stack is an ℓ-cohomologically smooth Artin v-stack of dimension zero.

ClassicalArithmeticCompletion:CA.0.summary: Divisibility, Euclidean algorithms and unique prime factorization lead to congruences, valuations and the Chinese remainder theorem. Arithmetic functions are organized by Dirichlet convolution and Möbius inversion, with applications to divisor sums. The Chinese remainder theorem for noncoprime moduli retains its compatibility condition.

ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES1.summary: Excursion operators connect functions on the stack of Langlands parameters with the center of the category of lisse sheaves and with Bernstein centers. Compact objects have a common finite wild-ramification cutoff; general noncompact objects need not. The stronger invariant-coordinate map requires the order of the component group of Z(G) to be invertible in the coefficient ring.

ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES6.title: Functoriality and duality of local Langlands parameters
ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES6.summary: Study how semisimple local Langlands parameters behave under isogenies, products, Weil restriction, character twists and central characters. For tori, the construction agrees with local class field theory with a fixed Frobenius normalization. Duality introduces the Chevalley involution, and pullbacks or exterior products are treated through their appropriate irreducible constituents.

ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES7.summary: Compare the geometric assignment of semisimple parameters with parabolic induction and with the classical local Langlands correspondence for GL_n. The parabolic comparison tracks the Levi cocycle, modulus character and Tate twists; characteristic-zero agreement over p-adic fields follows from cohomological realizations and trace comparisons. Semisimple parameters alone do not recover the monodromy operator of a Weil–Deligne representation.

FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums:FF.3.summary: Polynomial factorization over finite fields, irreducibility witnesses and Hensel lifting lead to certified algorithms for counting rational points. Complexity bounds distinguish bit operations from the use of randomness, and point counts are compared with cohomological trace formulas and proven error bounds.

GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS0.summary: Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannians classify modifications of G-bundles at varying divisors. Loop-group quotients, Beauville–Laszlo gluing and dominant cocharacters describe their Schubert cells, closures and dimensions. The geometry includes cohomological smoothness of open cells and projectivity of bounded Witt-vector Grassmannians, with integral models used under their required splitting hypotheses.

GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS3.summary: When modification points are disjoint, the Grassmannian factors into a product; allowing the points to collide produces fusion. Universally locally acyclic sheaves give the collision maps and their compatibility under repeated collisions. These constructions provide associativity, symmetry, units and finite-set functoriality, with signs and half-Tate twists fixed so that the cohomology functor is symmetric monoidal.

GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS4.summary: Reconstruct the Langlands dual group from the tensor category of Satake sheaves and its total-cohomology fibre functor. Weight functors and rank-one calculations identify the torus, root datum and integral group scheme, while descent supplies the Weil action. The equivalence is compared with Levi restriction, Verdier duality and the classical spherical Hecke algebra; rational semisimplicity is kept distinct from the integral theorem.

GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:.summary: Blichfeldt's theorem and Minkowski's first and second theorems relate the volume of a convex body to lattice points and successive minima. Their inequalities yield applications to ideal classes and units in number fields. Measurability, symmetry, lattice rank and boundary conventions remain explicit.

LanglandsParameterStacks:LP2.summary: Construct the excursion algebra from invariant functions on finite free-group cocycle spaces. Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from p, its characters determine conjugacy classes of continuous semisimple Langlands parameters with finite wild ramification. Comparing this algebra with the invariant-coordinate algebra of the parameter stack requires additional hypotheses for integral coefficients.

LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory:LD.0.summary: First-order languages for rings and valued fields provide structures, formulas, definable sets and interpretations in arithmetic fields. Ultraproducts and Łoś's theorem transfer statements between structures. Nonstandard arithmetic is formulated using explicit elementary extensions, with parameters and quantifier domains specified.

PadicHodgeTheory:P7.title: Robba rings and crystalline representation comparisons
PadicHodgeTheory:P7.summary: Construct bounded, overconvergent and Robba rings from convergent Laurent series on annuli, with their topologies, Frobenius and cyclotomic Γ-actions. Compare the resulting period constructions with étale (φ,Γ)-modules and Galois representations. For crystalline representations in the relevant weight and base-field range, relate Wach modules to filtered crystalline periods and integral lattices.

PerfectoidQuotients:Q0.summary: Integral perfectoid rings are related to Tate perfectoid rings through integral subrings and the A_inf and θ constructions. Perfect prisms provide an equivalent algebraic description involving δ-rings and Frobenius. Derived completion and simplicial commutative algebra are used with their flatness, regularity and torsion hypotheses.

QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM..summary: Theta functions, the Dedekind eta function and Jacobi forms combine transformation laws with Fourier expansions. Their weights, indices and multiplier systems connect integral and half-integral weight modular forms. Branch choices and cusp behavior are checked against the chosen metaplectic normalization.

Harmonic Maass forms are studied through the weight Laplacian, growth conditions and the holomorphic and nonholomorphic parts of their Fourier expansions. The ξ-operator relates these forms to their shadows. Poincaré series, pairings and exact sequences describe its kernel and image in the specified weight and growth spaces.

RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2.summary: Untilts determine Cartier divisors on relative Fargues–Fontaine spaces. Completion along a divisor produces local de Rham period rings and their filtrations, with residue fields identified at geometric untilts. Effective divisors, symmetric powers and Frobenius descent organize several modification points, including coincident points and the integral special fibre.

RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF4.summary: Beauville–Laszlo gluing reconstructs a vector bundle from its restriction away from a Cartier divisor, its formal completion and an identification on the punctured neighbourhood. The gluing equivalence respects tensor products, duals and base change. Tannakian descriptions extend this construction to G-torsors and their modifications.

ShimuraData:D0.summary: Weil restriction expresses the points of a group over a finite separable extension as the points of a group over the base field. Compare this construction on local and adelic topological points, including products and base change. Applications include the Deligne torus, Hilbert modular groups and morphisms of Shimura data.

VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2.summary: Positive twists give global generation and vanishing of higher cohomology, allowing comparison of bundles on analytic and schematic Fargues–Fontaine curves. At a geometric point, every vector bundle decomposes into stable bundles O(λ) indexed by rational slopes. Their ranks, degrees, Hom and Ext groups support the classification and Harder–Narasimhan filtrations; the isocrystal comparison here is a bijection on isomorphism classes.

VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3.title: Banach–Colmez spaces and spaces of sections
VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3.summary: Banach–Colmez spaces describe sections and cohomology of vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve. Positive line bundles and Lubin–Tate universal covers supply basic examples, while slope conditions control dimensions and cohomological smoothness. Projectivized section spaces and their properness are used to construct nowhere-zero sections in families.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/CombinatorialHeeg.title: The slice-genus bound
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/CombinatorialHeeg.summary: Prove that the absolute value of the grid-homology invariant τ is bounded by the slice genus of a knot. Construct saddle, birth and death maps and use normal forms of knot cobordisms to establish the bound.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/CombinatorialHeeg.title: Pointed Heegaard diagrams and admissibility
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/CombinatorialHeeg.summary: Describe pointed and multipointed Heegaard diagrams through their surface genus, attaching curves and basepoints. Construct generators, domains and periodic domains and define weak and strong admissibility in this combinatorial setting.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#mil.title: Gluing pseudoholomorphic curves
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#mil.summary: Construct gluing maps using pregluing, uniformly bounded right inverses, quadratic estimates and Newton iteration. Prove that the resulting families cover neighborhoods of broken configurations, completing the local description of compactified moduli spaces.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#mil.title: Symmetric products of Heegaard surfaces
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#mil.summary: Construct the smooth complex geometry of a Heegaard surface’s symmetric product and its totally real attaching tori. Study the second homotopy group in genus greater than two and the basepoint divisor, including positivity of its intersection with holomorphic disks.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#mil.title: The hat Floer complex and invariance
tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer#mil.summary: Define the hat Heegaard Floer differential over the field with two elements and prove that its square vanishes. Establish independence of the almost complex structure and invariance under isotopy, handleslides and stabilization using continuation maps and the specified torus-isotopy comparison.
